subject: Order form inspection cadence & pen-test coordination
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@clearbrookhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood order form — inspection cadence & pen-test language

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we finalize the order form I want to lock down a few items from our security review so my compliance team can close their checklist:

- SOC 2 report cadence: do you plan annual attestation or quarterly monitoring? We need to map to our vendor review calendar.
- Penetration testing: we need clear language on how pen-tests are coordinated (notice period, scope agreement, staging vs production access).
- Evidence and audit cadence: typical asks are sample logs, configuration exports, and an archived SOC2 report; what timeline can Redwood guarantee for delivery?
- Inspection scope: are inspection rights limited to SOC 2 / agreed artifacts or do you require broader on-site or live environment access?

We prefer limited inspection windows and an agreed playbook for evidence handoff — can you send proposed order form verbiage and any internal playbook that would help our reviewers?

Appreciate a short turnaround — we have a compliance gate on Aug 4.

Thanks,
Tom

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood order form — inspection cadence & pen-test language

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of what Redwood can commit to now (we'll loop legal for final MSA/order form language):

1) SOC 2: annual Type II attestation with a short-form summary snapshot (trust report) available on request. For higher-assurance timelines we can provide a rolling evidence window (last 12 months) via a secure share, deliverable within 5 business days of request.

2) Penetration testing: we don't allow unscheduled production testing. Proposed coordination: 14-day notice, mutually agreed scope, testing limited to non-prod (staging) unless customer signs a separate production-pen-test addendum and both parties agree on mitigations. We can require a code freeze / maintenance window if testing affects production services.

3) Evidence cadence: typical evidence delivery for the order form will be: SOC2 report (PDF), sample configuration snapshots, hashed logs for sampled windows, and a summary of remediation items. Delivery SLA: 5 business days for standard evidence items; 10 days for longer forensic exports.

4) Inspection rights: we propose limiting inspection to remote evidence exchange and scheduled staging access windows (48–72 hour windows) rather than open-ended on-site or live production access. Any deeper access should be scoped, scheduled, and documented.

Attached is an initial redlined order form draft and a short inspection playbook that maps evidence owners and expected artifacts. These are internal drafts — please review and tell us where you need tighter assurances.

Next step: I'll loop in our legal lead to convert the proposed bullets into contract language. If you have a template you prefer we can draft against that.

Attachments: redlined_orderform_draft.pdf (draft verbiage), inspection_playbook_v1.docx (operational playbook)

Best,
Olga

Thanks Olga — reviewed the attached playbook and redline. A few edits from a sales/ops perspective before we hand to legal:

- Add a 14-day mutual notice for pen-tests (matches Tom's ask) and require a signed scope doc prior to access.
- Clarify that staging environment access requires an account-level MFA and a scoped jumpbox — no direct root/console access to customer-facing production.
- Evidence delivery: propose a standard checklist we can push to the customer portal so requests are tracked; standard SLA should be 5 business days, but include an "expedited" 48–72 hour path for critical remediation requests (with associated fee or committed engineering support).
- Audit rights: strike any language that suggests continuous or unscheduled inspection; replace with "scheduled inspection windows" and a maximum of two remote windows per 12-month period unless otherwise agreed.

I've put comments into msaredline_comments_v2.docx — legal, can you please: 1) convert these bullets into contract-ready text, 2) review the operational constraints (staging only + jumpbox), and 3) confirm whether we should include an explicit pen-test non-disclosure / rules-of-engagement clause.

Proposed next step: Karthik + Olga + Tom — 30 min call next week to sign off on final wording and schedule the first evidence exchange.

Attachments: msaredline_comments_v2.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood order form — inspection cadence & pen-test language

Olga / Marissa / Tom —

Thanks — reviewed the thread and attachments. Below are contract-ready suggestions intended to balance Clearbrook's audit needs with Redwood's operational/security posture. I also attached a consolidated redline.

Key proposed clauses (high level):

1) Limited Inspection Rights: Customer may request access to compliance artifacts reasonably necessary to validate Redwood's compliance with the Security Exhibit (e.g., SOC 2 report, configuration snapshots, sample logs). Such requests shall be fulfilled via secure remote transfer and, where appropriate, scheduled staging access windows. Inspection rights shall not include unfettered on-site access to Redwood production environments or source code.

2) Scheduled Access Windows: Remote staging access will be granted in discrete windows of no more than 72 consecutive hours, scheduled at least 14 calendar days in advance, and mutually agreed. For time-sensitive investigations, an expedited access path (48–72 hour turnaround for evidence delivery) may be requested and will be accommodated at Redwood's discretion.

3) Penetration Testing: Customer-initiated penetration testing of Redwood services is permitted only upon (a) 14-day written notice, (b) execution of a mutually agreed Rules of Engagement (ROE) and Non-Disclosure Agreement for the engagement, and (c) agreement to limit testing to non-production environments unless an explicit production testing addendum is signed. Pen tests must not include privilege escalation to Redwood administrative accounts; any testing that could materially impact customer-facing services requires prior written consent.

4) Evidence SLAs and Acceptable Formats: Redwood will provide SOC2 reports (PDF) and requested samples (configuration dumps, hashed/log exports) within 5 business days of a validated request. For specialized forensic exports, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver within 10 business days. Evidence will be delivered via secure share; log exports will include integrity verifiers (hashes) and a short context note describing collection window and anonymization applied.

5) Limitation and Audit Frequency: Customer agrees that routine audits will be no more frequent than two scheduled remote access windows per 12-month period absent exceptional cause (e.g., incident or regulatory requirement). Additional audit windows may be agreed by mutual written consent.

6) Remedies and Remediation Tracking: Redwood will produce a remediation timeline for any findings within 10 business days and provide progress updates via the agreed customer portal until closure.

Operational notes:
- We should include a small section in the order form to reference the inspection_playbook_v1 (operational runbook) and attach it as a non-binding operational exhibit.
- Suggest adding an expedited evidence fee language for requests that require engineering hot-fix support outside normal SLAs.

I've attached msaredline_final_redlines.pdf with inline language for the MSA and an Order Form snippet you can paste into the customer order form. Legal caveats: we avoid any absolute wording that permits unlimited "inspection rights" — instead we define scope, frequency, format, and ROE.

Next steps: Tom, please confirm you and your compliance team are comfortable with the 14-day notice and two-windows-per-year limit; if yes, I'll prepare the final order form snippet and we can schedule the 30-min sign-off call next Tuesday (Aug 2) or Wednesday (Aug 3).

Cheers,
